video.title: EU4 1.35 Morocco Guide - RAIDING + GOLD MINES = OP ANDALUSIA

panels.title: Berber Iqta and raiding, all game

items.label: Iqta abilities
items.text: Start with Lenient Taxation (+1 diplomatic reputation, -15% liberty desire in subjects). Once it runs out, use the core-cost one (he takes it) or the tax one, whichever you need.

items.label: Raid coasts
items.text: Send light ships along the coast with shift-click, then press Raid in each sea tile for ducats and sailors. You can raid again every couple of years. Always keep raiding, it's an underrated income.

items.label: The Ottomans are your only ally
items.text: Ally them early and keep them. Whenever you declare on the Mamluks, call the Ottomans in so you control their truce and they don't take Egypt for themselves.

items.label: Corruption trick
items.text: On the Muslim event that lets you gain or lose corruption, debase currency for cash first, then pick the option that loses corruption.

phases.name: Day one setup
phases.intro: Everything here happens before you unpause. You start with three subjects (Tafilalt, Sous, Marrakesh) that you hold cores on, so they annex for free in 1454.

steps.text: Iqta ability: Lenient Taxation
steps.note: Subjects are rowdy. Over 50% liberty desire, the Iberians can back their independence

steps.text: Naval doctrine: Maghrebi Corsairs
steps.note: More privateer efficiency and loot. Swap to the galley combat doctrine before you fight the Iberians

steps.text: Summon the Diet
steps.note: Pick whichever agenda suits you

steps.text: Ulema: Religious State, Clerical Advisory Council, Religious Diplomats, Clerical Education
Amirs: Primacy of the Amirs, Increased Levies, Aristocratic Counselors
steps.note: They already have Strong Duchies. Integration Policy comes later, right before annexing subjects

steps.text: Merchants: Land of Commerce, Patronage of the Arts, Commercial Advisory Board, Indebted to the Merchant Guilds
steps.note: No Dhimmi privileges for now. Then seize land

steps.text: Hire three level 1 advisors even though you're losing money
steps.note: Admin: any (he takes national tax). Diplo: diplomatic reputation or improve relations. Mil: morale, discipline, fort defense or manpower (he takes manpower, you lose a lot to attrition). Raiding and the Tafilalt gold pay for it

steps.text: Hire the free company in Fez

chain: Shift-click your 5 light ships along every coastal sea tile
Press Raid in each tile as they arrive
steps.note: Ducats and sailors from every province in range

steps.text: Ally
steps.note: Only so they don't ally Tlemcen or Granada. Don't royal marry them

chain: Royal marry, or improve relations if you can't
Ally
steps.note: Your one real ally for the whole game

chain: Granada, with the free diplomat
Tlemcen, once the Tunis diplomat is back

steps.text: Rival whoever rivals you (Aragon, Castile, England in his game). He picks Portugal

phases.name: First war: Granada or Tlemcen
phases.intro: The crisis of the Maghreb event fires in the first month and hurts every Maghreb nation. Fight whichever of Granada or Tlemcen is easier.

loadout.note: Ten galleys on top of the army, even over naval force limit

chain: Build about 10 galleys with the raid money and sailors
Ally the Ottomans
Get claims on Granada and Tlemcen
Put your ruler in charge of the army
Hire an admiral and park the fleet off your target
steps.note: The starting ruler is bad, you want him to die. Claim even where Tafilalt has cores, it saves diplo points

steps.text: Declare on Granada if you can, otherwise Tlemcen
steps.note: He fought Tlemcen because Granada allied his ally Tunis

steps.text: Set subjects to Siege
If you end up at war with Fezzan, vassalize them
steps.note: Otherwise Tunis or the Mamluks usually get them before you border them

steps.text: Castile may annex Granada while you fight Tlemcen
steps.note: Normal, you'll take it later. If the follow-up event pops a new nation, pick the third option

chain: Full annex Tlemcen (or vassalize or annex Granada)
Keep Figuig yourself instead of giving it to Tafilalt
Take all their money
steps.note: Figuig would stop Tafilalt annexing on time since it isn't your core

phases.name: Mzab and Djerid
phases.intro: Wipe out Tlemcen and the small nations south of Tunis before Tunis gets to them.

have: Your three subjects heading to 190 opinion

steps.text: Improve relations with your three subjects to 190, and with your allies
steps.note: So you can annex them all the moment 1454 comes

chain: Spy network
Declare
Full annex
steps.note: Or whichever of Mzab and Djerid you border. If Tunis already ate them, break the Tunis alliance now

chain: Start spying while the last war is running
Declare
Full annex

steps.text: Break the alliance with Tunis when you start the last of these wars
steps.note: Keep it if you don't feel ready to face the Iberians with just the Ottomans

phases.name: Annex subjects and build up
phases.intro: December 1454 is the trigger. Your subjects annex in one month with no diplo points.

have: Tlemcen and the small southern nations annexed

chain: Recall all three diplomats in December 1454
Give the Amirs Integration Policy
Annex Tafilalt, Sous and Marrakesh
Wait for the month to tick
steps.note: They're at 100% immediately because you hold cores

steps.text: Full state their provinces

chain: Encourage Development edict in the Tafilalt state
Dev the gold mine to 10 production

steps.text: Lower autonomy, then trim the inherited fleet to what you can afford
steps.note: He deletes extra cogs and a light ship, sends 10 ships to privateer in Sevilla and keeps the war fleet docked. Being over force limit is fine if you can pay for it

steps.text: Raid every coastal province again
steps.note: Every couple of years

steps.text: Keep your forts if you're not sure you can stop invasions
steps.note: Delete them only if you're confident nobody crosses

steps.text: Spy on Tunis, keep improving relations with the Ottomans and curry favors

chain: Pay off the starting burgher loans
Take new burgher loans
Build marketplaces in every center of trade and estuary
steps.note: Any province giving more than 2 trade power: Tangier, Gharb, Tafilalt, Draa, Agadir, Tlemcen

steps.text: Admin tech 4: build mosques

chain: Reach tech 4 in every category
Encourage Development edict
Dev the capital or Tangier for the Renaissance
At 15 dev, expand infrastructure there
steps.note: It won't spread to you. He uses Tangier (cloth, level 2 center of trade). Core first, full state later with spare admin

steps.text: Tier 2 reform: Strengthen Noble Privileges
steps.note: Compromise with the Nobility if the Amirs' influence is already high. You need the manpower for attrition

phases.name: War with Tunis
phases.intro: Declare as soon as the truce from breaking the alliance runs out.

loadout.note: Don't fall a mil tech behind Tunis while you dev for the Renaissance
have: Tier 2 reform (Strengthen Noble Privileges, or Compromise with the Nobility if Amir influence is high)
Marketplaces in your centers of trade

chain: Check Tunis' allies
If they allied the Ottomans, spend favors to make the Ottomans drop them
steps.note: Rarely Tunis allies the Mamluks. Then fight the Mamluks with the Ottomans and add Tunis to that war

steps.text: Declare on Tunis
Wattasid Conspiracy event: first option
steps.note: You lose stability and pretender rebels rise, maybe more than once. Beat them so the mission branch moves on. Only let them win if their ruler is really good

chain: Give Fezzan back its core that Tunis took
Take the three centers of trade, Tripoli and Djerba among them
Take a bit more, leave Tunis a small rump
steps.note: No money or war reparations. You want a short truce to finish them later

steps.text: Fezzan: fight them if they still exist, or annex them at 190 if they're your vassal
Embrace the Renaissance
steps.note: Take loans if you need to. Don't sell it to Timbuktu, you'll fight them later

phases.name: Missions, forts and West Africa
phases.intro: Three routes open now: Iberia, Egypt and West Africa. Take whichever is easiest at any moment.

loadout.note: He's at mil tech 5 against Timbuktu's 3 by 1471
have: All of the Maghreb except Tunis

chain: Mosques (or 15 dev) in Fez, Marrakesh, Meknes and Gharb
Event: keep Fez as your capital
steps.note: Fez is a level 3 center of trade. He took loans for the mosques

steps.text: Saharan Route mission
steps.note: Caravan power, a core on Tuat and permanent claims in West Africa, where the gold mines are

steps.text: After the Wattasid resolution gives +1 stability, take the next mission, then Conquer Algiers
steps.note: Claims on land you mostly own already, then more privateer efficiency

steps.text: Swap the Iqta ability once Lenient Taxation runs out
steps.note: He takes the core-cost one. The tax one is the other option

steps.text: Admin tech 5: first idea group. Quality (he takes it) or Quantity
steps.note: Going colonial instead: Exploration, then Expansion. Quality if you manage armies carefully, Quantity to scale fast through desert attrition

chain: Tuat
Fezzan
On the Mamluk border
steps.note: So nobody walks into your core land

steps.text: Delete the inland forts, but keep one coastal fort as bait
steps.note: Enemies who siege it get trapped when your navy blocks the sea tile

steps.text: Take any easy war against Castile, Portugal or Aragon
steps.note: His Iberian alliances were too strong. Yours probably won't be

steps.text: Spy on the Mamluks for claims, and keep lowering autonomy after raids
Declare on whoever holds your West Africa claims (Timbuktu for him)
steps.note: They have big allies on paper but are far behind in tech

steps.text: Only the claimed provinces, no money, no war reparations
steps.note: The next mission gives more claims and you want short truces. If you full annex someone, take their money

steps.text: Claim Timbuktu mission

phases.name: Mamluks and Iberia
phases.intro: Juggle the three fronts. Hit the Mamluks with the Ottomans and look for an opening in Iberia.

have: First idea group (Quality or Quantity, or Exploration if colonial)
Forts in Tuat, Fezzan and on the Mamluk border

steps.text: Build a few more light ships to privateer
Declare on the Mamluks and call in the Ottomans
steps.note: Even if you could win alone. Declare before the Ottomans do, around the 1480s

steps.text: Tier 3 reform: Decentralized Bureaucracy
steps.note: +2 promoted cultures, minimum autonomy in territories and estate equilibrium

chain: Egyptian coast (Alexandria, Rashid, Damietta)
War reparations
All their money
steps.note: As much coast as your admin allows. You'll keep fighting them

steps.text: Swap the naval doctrine to galley combat ability
steps.note: The Iberians have strong navies. He says this on day one

chain: Build a sizable navy
Declare on Portugal
Hold Ceuta
White peace Castile and England when they get bored
Fight Portugal one on one for Ceuta and land in Iberia
steps.note: Or catch Aragon without strong allies. By the 1480s you could own southern Iberia and form Andalusia

steps.text: Full annex what's left of Tunis
Spy on whoever took Maghreb land (Genoa for him) for when the truce ends
Convert Ibadi provinces once you have the missionary strength
steps.note: No rush

steps.text: Promote Algerian and Tunisian

chain: Take new burgher loans
Marketplaces in centers of trade and estuaries
Workshops in high-value trade good provinces
steps.note: Planning for later, when autonomy, culture and religion catch up

steps.text: Upgrade every great project you own once you're rich
steps.note: Your starting one, the Holy City of Kairouan from Tunis and the Great Mosque of Djenne are all strong at tier 3. Not a priority yet

steps.text: Admin tech 7: second idea group, Trade
steps.note: Colonial: Expansion instead. You can't make trade companies from Africa, so merchants have to come from ideas

steps.text: Third merchant: transfer or collect near the Sevilla node
steps.note: He collects in Alexandria for now. Once you form Andalusia the capital moves and Sevilla becomes your home node

steps.text: Admin tech 8: courthouses everywhere
steps.note: You'll be over governing capacity by now

chain: Declare when the truce ends
Take the three provinces they took from Tunis
Take a little cash
steps.note: He also took Corsica as a foot in the door in Italy

chain: Declare for the claimed provinces
Separate peace Timbuktu for its claimed province
Take the claimed provinces and some money
steps.note: Songhai keeps up on tech through their missions. Your Tuat fort is what stops them walking through your land

steps.text: Sahel Campaign mission, then invade Mali, Kanem and Benin as the missions say
steps.note: Permanent claims across the Niger and Sahel. Fight whoever is weakest, no new allies needed

steps.text: Declare on the Mamluks again when the truce ends, with the Ottomans
Tier 4 reform: Strengthen the Ulema
steps.note: If you plan to convert. Otherwise Curtail Clerical Privileges, or Maintain Balance of Power for a diplomat

steps.text: Mamluk coast and high-dev provinces, plus money
Once big, diplo-vassalize minors where you plan to expand next, like Italy

phases.name: 1509 benchmarks
phases.intro: Where you should be when colonialism spawns.

steps.text: Realm: all of the Maghreb, a foothold in the Sahel and in Egypt, maybe part of Iberia and Andalusia formed
Buildings: marketplaces in every center of trade and estuary, workshops in high-value goods, plenty of mosques, a few army buildings
Army: 24 infantry / 4 cavalry / 7 artillery, costing about 13 ducats a month
steps.note: He could afford to double it and still make about 17 ducats profit

steps.text: Income mostly from tax, production and gold
steps.note: Trade stays low until you move to the Sevilla node

steps.text: Third idea group: whichever of Quality and Quantity you didn't take
steps.note: Colonial: Exploration, Expansion, then the same as below

steps.text: Fourth: Administrative or Diplomatic for expansion, Economic or Infrastructure for money, or Humanist or Religious for stability
Tier 5: Organized Military Staff or Military Engineering
Tier 6: Aristocratic Court, then Royal Decree once absolutism spawns
Tier 7: Meritocratic Recruitment
steps.note: Colonial: the colonial companies option

steps.text: Tier 8: Empower the Burghers or Embrace Economic Theory
steps.note: Colonial: Exploitation of the New World

steps.text: Tier 9: depends on your subjects. Tiers 10 and 11: any
Keep pushing the Mamluks, calling in the Ottomans every time
Conquer the Sahel, Niger and Guinea and dev the other gold mines
Form Andalusia and move the capital to the Sevilla node, then route trade there
Colonial runs: trade companies on the Ivory Coast, South Africa and Zanzibar
Egypt for sure, the Mashriq and Arabia if your goals go there. The Horn of Africa isn't needed
Get every great project you own to tier 3, including the Iberian ones
